framework: CRITICAL: Do not treat asymptomatic bacteriuria in a catheterized patient — pyuria and bacteriuria are nearly universal with long-term catheterization and do NOT by themselves indicate infection requiring antibiotics.
Replace the catheter (not just treat through it) as part of source control when initiating treatment for symptomatic CA-UTI — this improves response and reduces relapse.

Reassess ongoing need for the catheter itself at every encounter — removing unnecessary catheters is the single most effective prevention strategy and a core stewardship action independent of any single infection episode.

Send urine culture before starting antibiotics whenever feasible, ideally from a freshly placed/replaced catheter, since cultures from long-standing catheters often reflect colonization rather than the infecting organism alone.
